about: This prayer asks that receiving the Body of Christ bring neither judgment nor condemnation, but protection and healing. Its wording recalls 1 Corinthians 11:29, where Saint Paul warns against receiving unworthily.

seg.tr: The reception of Your Body, Lord Jesus Christ, which I, though unworthy, dare to receive,

fn.w003: Genitive neuter singular agreeing with Córporis.
fn.w007: Neuter relative pronoun referring to Córporis.
fn.w008: Nominative subject of præsúmo, expressed for emphasis.
fn.w009: Nominative masculine singular agreeing with ego.
fn.w011: Præsúmo here means to venture or dare to receive.

seg.tr: may it bring me neither judgment nor condemnation:

fn.w014: Third-person present subjunctive. Provénio here means to turn out or result.
fn.w016: The word used in 1 Corinthians 11:29 for unworthy reception.

seg.tr: but because of Your goodness, may it protect my mind and body and bring me healing:

fn.w022: Here “pro” (w020) with the ablative expresses the ground of the petition: because of Thy loving-kindness.
fn.w023: Shares its subject with provéniat and states the positive outcome requested.
fn.w026: Accusative after ad, governing the two genitives that follow.
fn.w027: Genitive dependent on tutaméntum and paired with córporis.
fn.w033: A gerundive agreeing with “medélam” (w032). With ad it expresses purpose.

seg.tr: who, being God, live and reign with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit for ever and ever. Amen.
